I can't confirm that. The evidence is insufficient for the full period (2026-10-05 to 2026-11-04).

NASA FIRMS recorded zero thermal detections intersecting the property on the days covered, which run from 2026-10-05 through 2026-11-03 for all four sensors (MODIS and three VIIRS satellites). The final day, 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-04, is not covered. The latest near-real-time data file hadn't yet included it, so a fire on that day would not show up.

Even for the covered days, "no detections" doesn't prove "no fire." Small, short-lived, cool, or cloud-obscured fires may go undetected. The result also says nothing about burned area or about anything outside this period.

Once the data for the last day is published, the check can be rerun to close the gap.
